To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have solved the crystal structure of the catalytic C‐terminus of the catalytic Pol α subunit (Pol2p) bound to the B (Pol31p) subunit of Pol α, and we have solved an EM reconstruction of Pol α that reveals a bilobal structure with a separate catalytic and B subunit‐containing module.

the B subunits of eukaryotic replicative DNA polymerase form a heterodimer that is a conserved structural and functional unit shared by all three replicative DNA polymerizes and that the B subunite is tethered to a separate polymerase domain through an unstructured linker.
the B–CTDs of the replicative DNA polymerase subunits are structurally conserved and that the catalytic and regulatory subunits are tethered together through a flexible linker.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure and function of DNA replication enzymes.
the structural and mechanistic basis of DNA polymerase activity, replication fidelity and DNA damage tolerance.
the structural and functional characterization of multi-subunit polymerases that are responsible for genome replication and DNA repair in all eukaryotes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the B subunits of the replicative polymerases are the functional core of these enzymes and that the B subdomain of the catalytic Pol α CTD is the key structural element for the assembly of Pol α.

this work describes the structure of the B–C-terminal domain (CTD)-containing subunit (B–CTD subunit) of yeast DNA polymerase α (Pol α) at 1.8-Å resolution, as well as the 3D architecture and subunit arrangement of Pol α by electron microscopy (EM).
the B subunits of Pol α, Pol ε, and Pol δ are tethered to the catalytic subunits via flexible linkers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the structure of Pol α reveals a mechanism of accessory factor interaction that is conserved in the three major eukaryotic replicative polymerases.

the structure of the catalytic B subunit is highly conserved among the three replicative polymerase complexes, whereas the CTD of the catalytic Pol α subunit is unique and represents an important element of the functional architecture of this replicative polymerase complex.
we describe the 3D architecture and the subunit interactions of Pol α and show that this polymerase is a heterodimeric protein with a bilobal architecture.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the conserved catalytic core is tethered to a flexible regulatory domain through a structured linker, which provides an architectural framework to accommodate accessory subunits and regulatory factors.
we have solved the structure of the C-terminal domain of the catalytic Pol α subunit (Pol1) bound to the regulatory Pol α subunit B (Cdc17).

the catalytic and regulatory domains of the B subunit are tethered to each other by a flexible linker that allows the B subunit to adopt different conformations in the context of different DNA polymerase complexes.
